findings.title: Prometheus join by private IP cannot match db-mon-1, so the node table is falsely red on day one
findings.quote:
The node table is joined to Prometheus target health by private IP; a target that
is absent is `red` with `"no node_exporter target"`.
findings.claim: FLEET.md gives db-mon-1 private 10.20.0.30, but Prometheus scrapes it as host.docker.internal:9100. There is no 10.20.0.30 node_exporter target in the evidence, so the plan's own absent-target rule marks the box that hosts NFS/Postgres/Redis/Prometheus red while its exporter is up.
findings.impact: The page's headline becomes '9 nodes, 1 red' forever, and the Prometheus card simultaneously says 9/9 targets up. The operator's first action is to chase a healthy db-mon-1, which is exactly the noise the page was built to remove; acceptance step 5's '8/9 targets up' also cannot be reconciled with the node table.
findings.fix: Match targets on the instance host OR the node's public IP, and add an explicit alias for host.docker.internal -> db-mon-1 (or scrape db-mon-1 via 10.20.0.30:9100 from the mesh). Best: derive the node list from target labels instead of hardcoding FLEET.md.

findings.title: A hung NFS statfs starves the web process's threadpool; the 1200 ms race bounds the response, not the damage
findings.quote:
- `statfs` on a hard-mounted NFS can block in the kernel; the 1200 ms race
  returns a red result but the request thread may stay until the mount recovers.
findings.claim: fs.promises.statfs runs on libuv's threadpool (4 threads by default). Promise.race and AbortSignal time out the promise, not the kernel call, and the 5 s cache starts a fresh statfs every 5 s. After ~20 s of a hung hard mount the pool is exhausted, and every fs and getaddrinfo call in the web process queues behind it - including express.static and the mtime store read (admin/api.js:160).
findings.impact: When NFS hangs, the page that exists to report it stalls the web tier serving the capture page: assets stop loading, /api/admin/health itself times out, and the operator loses the one signal they opened the page for. At 3 a.m. with nobody watching, a single mount hang becomes a web outage, not a red row.
findings.fix: Run statfs out of process (df -P on the mount, or a child node process) and kill it at the budget; or a worker_thread you terminate. Keep at most one statfs in flight (skip scheduling while one is outstanding) and serve the last-good result marked stale.

findings.title: The workers check promises per-role coverage the socket pool cannot compute
findings.quote: | workers | >= 1 per expected role | fewer than expected | 0 |
findings.claim: The plan feeds this from WorkerPool.snapshot() 'from its existing maps (same numbers already emitted in admin:ready)'. Those numbers are slotStats() = {workers, auth, export, queued}; worker:ready carries only slot counts and addWorker stores only {socket, slots, connectedAt}. No hostname, node id or role reaches the pool, so 'per expected role' is unimplementable as written and degrades to a hardcoded total.
findings.impact: The worker tier cannot say which role or node is missing, and a hardcoded 7 drifts with the fleet. With 2 download + 5 OCR workers, a total check can read green while the OCR role is gone, or red with no way to localise it - the second half of the page's question ('which dependency is failing') is lost.
findings.verification_command: grep -n 'worker:ready' python/worker/__main__.py; grep -n -A6 'addWorker(socket)' server/socket/worker-pool.js; grep -n -A8 'slotStats()' server/socket/worker-pool.js
findings.fix: Have the worker send its node id or role in worker:ready (or map socket.handshake.address through fleet.js privateIp), or drop 'per role' and state the check as 'total >= EXPECTED_WORKERS' with an explicit config value.

findings.title: Postgres and Redis checks have no configured host or credential in the web process
findings.quote:
- `probeRedis(url, password)` — raw RESP `AUTH` (if a password is set) then
  `PING`; accepts `+PONG`; reads at most 256 bytes.
findings.claim: The plan never says where url/password come from. server/config.js has no redis or postgres section (config object is admin/geo/telegram/store/worker/icloud, 59-154) and .env.example has no REDIS/POSTGRES keys. FLEET.md puts REDIS_PASSWORD and DB_PASSWORD only on db-mon-1; the web runs on session-1 whose secret list omits both.
findings.impact: On day one the Redis check sends no AUTH, gets NOAUTH, and by the plan's own table (line 46) that is yellow forever; Postgres has no host/port source either. Two of nine checks are permanent noise, so overall never clears even after the gate is fixed, or a live secret gets pasted into server code.
findings.fix: Add REDIS_URL/REDIS_PASSWORD and PG_HOST/PG_PORT to config.js and .env.example, and state that the values are copied to session-1's env; treat NOAUTH as red ('server requires auth, we have no password'), not yellow.

findings.title: The new unauthenticated /healthz is published on a listener bound to all interfaces, not loopback
findings.claim: socket/index.js calls httpServer.listen(config.socketPort, cb) with no host, which binds ::/0.0.0.0; only the log string at 110 says 127.0.0.1, and map.md:27 repeats that log as if it were the bind. The plan then adds worker/slot counts and the account count to that listener with no auth.
findings.impact: Any host that can reach 4001 on session-1 (UFW permitting) reads fleet capacity and account count without a session - the 'read-only, admin-only' posture the panel otherwise keeps. Low sensitivity today with one account, but it is a new unauthenticated surface added for a number the admin SPA already receives.
findings.fix: httpServer.listen(port, '127.0.0.1') (nginx proxies from the same host), or return only {ok,uptime} unauthenticated and keep counts behind the admin route. Correct map.md:27 to say the bind is unspecified/all-interfaces.
